scenes.say: In 1919, a giant wave of syrup tore through Boston at thirty five miles an hour.
A huge steel tank stood in the North End, holding over two million gallons of molasses.
It had leaked from the start. Then, on January fifteenth, it burst.
A wave about twenty five feet high crushed buildings and bent the steel of an elevated railway.
It moved at thirty five miles an hour. Nobody could outrun it.
Twenty one people died, and about one hundred and fifty were hurt.
The cleanup took weeks, and the disaster led to stricter building rules across America.
